evidence.claim: DC flux biasing (currents uniform in [-1,1] mA) dissipates on average 0.050(3) uW per flux line on the MXC; 25 flux lines give 1.25(7) uW on MXC, about 15 times below the MXC cooling power at 20 mK.
evidence.document_title: Engineering cryogenic setups for 100-qubit scale superconducting circuit systems
evidence.quote: dissipated, evaluating to 0.050(3) μW (0.140(7) μW) on MXC (CP). For 25 flux lines this sums up to 1.25(7) μW (3.5(2) μW) on MXC (CP), which is about a factor of 15 (40) smaller than the cooling power available at MXC (CP) at a temperature of 20 mK (140 mK).
evidence.value_as_printed: 0.050(3) μW per line; 1.25(7) μW for 25 lines

evidence.applies_to: Cryocoolers in general; measured on a Cryomech PT415 pulse tube in the PB-2b receiver
evidence.claim: Every cryocooler has a load curve/capacity map relating the maximum heat load it can remove to its operating temperature; loads above the nominal operating point drive the stage to a higher temperature, and the base temperature is set by the balance between cooling capacity and parasitic load.
evidence.document_title: Design and characterization of the POLARBEAR-2b and POLARBEAR-2c cosmic microwave background cryogenic receivers
evidence.location: Section 2.1 '50 K and 4 K Refrigeration', p. 3-4 (arXiv v1)
evidence.quote: For all cryocoolers there is a relation between the maximum heat load that they can dissipate and their operating temperature, known as a load curve, or in a two-parameter space, a capacity map.

evidence.applies_to: Pulse tube cryocooler (PT415) stages; general steady-state cryostat heat balance
evidence.claim: Heat loads above (below) a cryocooler's operating point give higher (lower) stage temperatures; the base temperature is a balance of cooling capacity and parasitic loading (steady-state heat balance).
evidence.document_title: Design and characterization of the POLARBEAR-2b and POLARBEAR-2c cosmic microwave background cryogenic receivers
evidence.location: Section 2.1 '50 K and 4 K Refrigeration'; see also Figure 4 (load curve of PT415 second stage, base 2.54 K at 0 W)
evidence.quote: Heat loads above (below) these operating points results in higher (lower) system temperatures [...] The lowest temperature reached by each stage of the PTC is referred to as the base temperature, which is a balance of the PTC cooling capacity and the parasitic loading.
